CRLR No.600 of 2024
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. Chetan Joshi, Advocate for the 
revisionist. 
2. Mr. G.S. Sandhu, Addl. A.G. with Ms. 
Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder for the State.
3. Learned counsel for the revisionist would 
submit that this revision is filed against the 
order dated 05.08.2024 passed by Chief Judicial 
Magistrate, Dehradun, whereby the application 
filed by the revisionist u/s 216 of Cr.P.C. for 
framing of additional charges u/s 120-B, 409 & 
471 of IPC against the respondent no.2/accused 
has been dismissed.
4. He would further submit that a bare 
perusal of evidence on record would clearly 
reveal that the commission of offence under 
Sections 120-B, 409 and 471 of IPC is made out 
but neither the said sections were added in the 
F.I.R. nor in the charge-sheet and nor charges 
under said sections were framed against the 
respondent no.2/accused and when the 
revisionist filed application for framing of 
additional charge under these charges, the same 
was also rejected by the Magistrate, without 
application of judicial mind.
5. He would further submit that the 
evidences and the arguments are over in the 
trial court but the judgment is yet not 
pronounced. 
6. Issue notice to the respondent no.2  through ordinary and registered post 
acknowledgment due as well as by Email and 
WhatsApp, if available.
7. Steps to be taken within two weeks.
8. List on 23.12.2024.
9. Till the next date of listing, further 
proceedings of Criminal Case No.1213/2015 
“State vs. Bharat Bhusan Batra” pending 
before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, 
Dehradun shall remain stayed. (Stay 
Application IA No.1/2024 is disposed of).
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 19.09.2024
Rajni

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 600 of 2024
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. V.B. S. Negi, learned Sr. Advocate assisted 
by Mr. Chetan Joshi, learned counsel for the 
revisionists.
2. Mr. Sandeep Sharma and Mr. Himanshu Sain, 
learned AGA for the State.
3. Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel for the 
respondent no. 2. 
4. Learned Sr. Advocate for the revisionist has 
placed reliance on the judgment of Hon’ble Supreme 
Court in the case of Anant Prakash Sinha Vs. State of 
Haryana and another (2016) 6 SCC 105 particularly 
on paragraphs no. 2, 6 and 22 and by referring this 
judgment, learned Sr. Advocate submits that in view 
of the aforesaid judgment, it cannot be said that 
application moved by the complainant for alteration of 
charge is not maintainable. He further submits that in 
view of the aforesaid judgment, at least the trial court 
should examine the material produced by the 
complainant and apply its judicial mind before 
rejecting the application but in the present case the 
trial court has rejected the application in a very 
cursory and casual manner without examining the 
material.
5. Learned counsel for both the parties also placed 
reliance on an another judgment of Hon’ble Supreme 
Court in the case of P. Karikalakshmi Vs. Sri Ganesh 
and another (2017) 3 SCC 347, particularly, by placing 
reliance to paragraph 6 and 7 of the judgment. 
6. List on 07.04.2026 for further arguments. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 24.03.2026
SKS
